blockers.summary: Section 4.1 tells adults that a search of their own diagnosis returns nothing they could join, and the trial it cites in the same breath admits adults. NCT06239272 enrols ages 1-30; an adult is 18 or over; the 18-30 band is both. The paper's own sentence supplies the premise that refutes its conclusion.
blockers.where: Section 4.1, final sentence of the paragraph beginning 'The mechanism therefore runs in both directions'.
blockers.quote: 'One record does both, and it bounds the claim: NCT06239272 carries the histology among its 42 listed conditions and is a recruiting interventional trial, so nothing here says that no listing anywhere names this disease and admits it. It enrols ages 1 to 30, so for an adult patient a search of the diagnosis still returns nothing they could join.'
blockers.evidence: research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> task_1_reverification_of_section_3_3.trials, the NCT06239272 record: overall_status 'RECRUITING', phases ['PHASE1','PHASE2'], interventions ['Surgical resection','Proton beam radiation therapy','Pazopanib','Ifosfamide','Doxorubicin','Selinexor'], maximum_age '30 Years', listed_conditions of length 42 including the literal string 'Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma', emc_in_listed_conditions true, and verbatim_eligibility_sentence (with verbatim_sentence_is_transport_clean true): 'Inclusion Criteria - All Patients * Patients must be 1-30 years at the time of the biopsy that established the diagnosis of NRSTS.' Every one of the paper's factual statements about this record checks out - 42 conditions, recruiting, interventional, ages 1 to 30. Only the inference fails: a 25-year-old adult with this diagnosis is inside 1-30, searches the histology, and gets back a recruiting interventional trial that lists it. The criterion is also anchored to age AT THE DIAGNOSTIC BIOPSY, not age at enrolment, which widens the admitted set further - a patient now 33 who was biopsied at 29 is not excluded by the sentence as retrieved.
blockers.why_a_reader_would_be_misled: This is the single most actionable sentence in the paper and it points the wrong way. A young-adult patient or their clinician, reading a paper whose thesis is that searching your diagnosis is futile, is told explicitly that their own search is futile - at the exact moment the paper is describing the trial that would have answered it. The paper's harm model (section 4, 'a map that sends a patient toward a trial that will refuse them is worse than no map') has a mirror image, and this sentence is it: telling a patient not to look for a trial that would take them.
blockers.fix: Replace 'for an adult patient' with the bound the record actually sets - 'for a patient over 30' - and state that the cap is on age at diagnostic biopsy rather than at enrolment. The sentence then says something true and keeps the concession it was written to make.

blockers.where: research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md (§4.1, final sentence of the bounding paragraph)
blockers.quote: It enrols ages 1 to 30, so for an adult patient a search of the diagnosis still returns nothing they could join.
blockers.why: The cited artifact refutes the clause it is built on. research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> task_1_reverification_of_section_3_3, NCT06239272 records maximum_age '30 Years', minimum_age null, and verbatim_eligibility_sentence 'Inclusion Criteria - All Patients * Patients must be 1-30 years at the time of the biopsy that established the diagnosis of NRSTS.' with verbatim_sentence_is_transport_clean true. An adult aged 18-30 is inside that range, so for such a patient a search of the diagnosis DOES return a recruiting interventional trial (NCT06239272, emc_in_listed_conditions true, 42 listed conditions including 'Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma') that they could join. On the verbatim wording the bound is age AT BIOPSY, not age now, so it is looser still. This is the one sentence that keeps the paper's headline framing intact against the single record that both names and admits the disease - the sentence immediately before it concedes 'nothing here says that no listing anywhere names this disease and admits it', and then this clause takes the concession back for every adult. A reachability paper is read by patients and clinicians; a false 'nothing you could join' is the error this paper's own §4 argues costs the most.
blockers.fix: It enrols only to age 30 - 'Patients must be 1-30 years at the time of the biopsy that established the diagnosis' - so for a patient diagnosed after 30, which is most of this disease's incidence, a search of the diagnosis still returns nothing they could join.

blockers.summary: 'No search of their own diagnosis will ever return' (front-matter purpose, abstract twice) and the title's 'unfindable' are UNIVERSAL claims about search, and the paper never ran the search. It ran condition searches (query.cond) and gene-term searches (query.term), and never a free-text search for the disease name against the two trials it says are unfindable.
blockers.evidence: §1 defines the mechanism by fiat — 'Listed conditions are what a search matches' — and no instrument in §2 or in the deposit tests that definition. The paper's own data contradicts the narrow model: the deposited NR4A3 term search (query.term=NR4A3) returns a neck-pain trial, two whey-protein trials and a spinal-cord-injury trial whose conditions fields are 'Neck Pain', 'Healthy/Young/Elderly' and 'Spinal Cord Injuries' — so ClinicalTrials.gov's term search demonstrably matches text OUTSIDE the conditions field. If NCT05918640's or NCT06571734's free text names the histology anywhere, the title claim is false; the paper does not say, and the deposit records no such check.
blockers.what_would_settle_it: One $0 CI fetch: query.term='extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma' (and the hyphenated variant) against ClinicalTrials.gov, recording totalCount and whether NCT05918640 / NCT06571734 appear. It will most likely come out the paper's way — which is exactly why running it converts an asserted premise into a measured one. If it is not run, 'no search' must be scoped to 'no condition search' everywhere it appears, including the title's logic.

blockers.summary: 'The driver gene is absent from the index entirely' (§3) and 'The sharpest result is an absence' (abstract) are stated at maximum strength on a query the paper's own deposit describes as returning a sample rather than an enumeration, and no totalCount was recorded.
blockers.evidence: fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json → task_2_widened_search.limits_of_this_screen[0], verbatim: 'The registry-wide EWSR1 term search returns full records and is therefore capped by response size, not by pageSize: 7 studies came back for pageSize=100. It is a sample of EWSR1-indexed trials, not an enumeration.' The NR4A3 query is the IDENTICAL form — https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies?query.term=NR4A3&pageSize=100&format=json — so the same cap applies, and the nr4a3_is_absent_from_the_registry_index block records five study records and NO totalCount. Whether the cap bound at five is UNKNOWN and unrecorded. The paper discloses none of this: grep of the pinned text finds no 'totalCount', no 'sample', no 'enumerat' (the one hit is §5 about protocols), no page-size or response-size caveat anywhere in §2 or §5. §3 also self-contradicts across two sentences: 'absent from the index entirely' followed immediately by 'A term search for it returns five studies'.
blockers.what_would_settle_it: Re-fetch recording totalCount (or use a fielded query with fields= so the cap is pageSize rather than response size). Failing that, both sentences must be scoped to what the capped query returned — 'the five records this query returned' — and the response-size cap added to §5. CLAUDE.md's own rule applies verbatim here: an absence of registry records is not an absence of trials.

blockers.summary: §4.1, lines 164-165: 'It enrols ages 1 to 30, so for an adult patient a search of the diagnosis still returns nothing they could join.' The inference does not follow from the paper's own number. An adult is 18 or over; NCT06239272 enrols 1-30; adults aged 18-30 are inside the range. The sentence tells that group there is nothing for them, and it is the paper's only sentence that speaks directly to a patient's situation.
blockers.evidence: The paper states the age range itself ('ages 1 to 30'). fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json → task_1 trials[1]: NCT06239272, maximum_age '30 Years', overall_status RECRUITING, emc_in_listed_conditions TRUE, 42 listed conditions, INTERVENTIONAL, verbatim inclusion criterion 'Patients must be 1-30 years at the time of the biopsy that established the diagnosis of NRSTS.' So a recruiting interventional trial that LISTS the histology admits adults up to 30, and a diagnosis search returns it. The error runs in the harmful direction — it understates a young adult's options — in a paper the brief flags as one a patient or clinician might act on.
blockers.what_would_settle_it: Two words: 'for a patient over 30'. If the paper wants the broader statement it must carry EMC's age distribution with a citation, which it currently does not report at all.

blockers.summary: §4.1: 'It enrols ages 1 to 30, so for an adult patient a search of the diagnosis still returns nothing they could join.' The trial admits adults aged 18-30, so the absence is false for that population, and it is the paper's most actionable sentence.
blockers.evidence: emc-trial-reachability.md line 164-165. The paper's own cited artifact, research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> task_1_reverification_of_section_3_3.trials[1]: nct_id NCT06239272, overall_status 'RECRUITING', maximum_age '30 Years', emc_in_listed_conditions true, 42 listed_conditions, memo_claim_checked 'verified open and EMC-eligible; EMC an explicitly listed condition; ages 1-30'. Adults are people aged 18 and over; the interval 18-30 is non-empty and, in a sarcoma whose paediatric-and-young-adult protocols are a live route, it is not a negligible slice. The method supports at most 'for an adult over 30'. The error runs in the harmful direction: it tells an adult patient that searching their own diagnosis is futile when for anyone aged 18-30 the paper's own record shows it is not.

blockers.summary: Every absence about what a diagnosis search returns rests on condition-search payloads that provably dropped records, and §2 discloses only the character-loss half of the transport defect. Seven NCT ids lost to that defect are never resolved anywhere in the three artifacts §7 names, and three of the seven were returned by the diagnosis searches themselves.
blockers.evidence: emc-trial-reachability.md lines 111-116 describe only that 'eligibility text containing them lost characters' and the resulting quoting rule; the strings 'unparse', 'module', 'dropped' and any count of lost records appear nowhere in the manuscript (grep over the pinned file returns nothing). The cited sweep's transport_integrity block names two failure modes, the second being 'SILENT and more dangerous: the record still parses while whole modules have vanished'. Enumerated there: unparseable_records.ct_emc_all (url query.cond=extraskeletal+myxoid+chondrosarcoma) lost NCT00720174 and NCT05355753; unparseable_records.ct_myxoid_chondrosarcoma (query.cond=myxoid+chondrosarcoma) lost NCT00720174, NCT05355753 and NCT01189253; silently_damaged_records shows NCT05836571 returned from ct_emc_all and ct_myxoid_chondrosarcoma with conditionsModule, designModule and eligibilityModule all missing, and NCT01189253 the same from ct_emc_all. Across the sweep 12 distinct NCT ids were lost to the defect; 5 are recoverable from another payload in the same file; 7 are not resolved anywhere in fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json, emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json or non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json: NCT00720174, NCT01189253, NCT02180867, NCT02736565, NCT04094610, NCT05355753 and NCT05697874. Three of those seven - NCT00720174, NCT05355753 and NCT01189253 - are records a diagnosis condition search returned and that were never read, which is exactly the set that decides what such a search returns. An absence stated about the output of a search cannot exceed the records that search delivered AND that were read; the manuscript states the absence and names neither the loss nor its size.

p1s.summary: The §3 table prints NCT06571734's listed conditions as a five-item list and the registry field has seven items — 'Ewing Sarcoma' is in the field and not in the paper's cell. The paper prints NCT05918640's four listed conditions completely one row above, and the abstract prints them completely again, so a reader has every reason to read these cells as the whole field. The omission is not neutral: the paper's own §4 counter-finding is about Ewing-sarcoma keyword traps, and a reader who opens the record finds Ewing sarcoma listed on the very trial the paper offers as the clean admitting example.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: The claim the cell supports — EMC is absent from the field — is true either way, and the two leiomyosarcoma entries being merged into 'metastatic and unresectable leiomyosarcoma' is a fair compression.
p1s.fix: Add 'Ewing sarcoma' to the cell, or mark the cell as a partial list.
p1s.evidence: research/literature/emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json, adjudications[NCT06571734].listed_conditions = ['Metastatic Leiomyosarcoma','Unresectable Leiomyosarcoma','Bone Sarcoma','Translocation-associated Soft Tissue Sarcoma','Synovial Sarcomas','Osteosarcoma Metastatic','Ewing Sarcoma'] (7 entries)

p1s.summary: The abstract says the nine further registry records 'name no histology either'. Seven of the nine name at least one specific disease in their conditions field — 45 named-disease condition entries across the nine, from NCT07440290's nineteen-item list down to NCT05770102's ten — and one of them, NCT06988475, lists 'Soft Tissue Sarcoma', a class term that covers this disease. Only NCT05722886 ('Haematological Malignancy', 'Solid Tumour') and NCT03767075 ('Advanced Solid Tumor') name no disease at all.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: The 'either' plausibly carries the referent from the preceding sentence ('neither lists it'), so the intended reading is 'name no such histology' — and the §3 table cell states it correctly as 'various; none names this histology'. The abstract is the loose restatement of a body cell that is right.
p1s.fix: 'name this histology no more than the first two do', or simply 'do not name it either'.
p1s.evidence: fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json, task_2_widened_search.molecularly_defined_not_histology_defined[*].listed_conditions

p1s.summary: §3 asserts 'The driver gene is absent from the index entirely', resting on a term search that the cited artifact classifies as a sample rather than an enumeration. That artifact's limits_of_this_screen[0] says a registry-wide term search returning full records is 'capped by response size, not by pageSize: 7 studies came back for pageSize=100. It is a sample of EWSR1-indexed trials, not an enumeration.' The NR4A3 search is the same instrument at the same pageSize, so its five results carry the same cap, and five results cannot establish absence 'entirely'. The paper carries none of that limit — §5 lists five limitations and this is not among them.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: The two sentences around it are correctly scoped to what the search returned ('a term search for the driver gene returns five studies', 'No trial that search returns is indexed to this disease's driver'), and both re-derive exactly. Five results also came back under a cap that admitted seven elsewhere, which is weak evidence against truncation. The overreach is one adverb on a correct paragraph.
p1s.fix: Drop 'entirely', or add the source artifact's own caveat that a full-record term search is a size-capped sample.
p1s.evidence: fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json, task_2_widened_search.limits_of_this_screen[0] and nr4a3_is_absent_from_the_registry_index.studies (5 records, none truncated: the NR4A3 payload appears in neither unparseable_records nor silently_damaged_records)

p1s.summary: §2 and the §3 table both say eligibility text was retrieved 'individually' for three of the nine basket records. Three of the nine carry eligibility_text_retrieved = true, but only two of those came from a per-NCT URL: NCT05722886 and NCT03767075. The third, NCT06988475, came from the bulk screen ct_sarcoma_2026_new, whose source_url is a query (query.cond=sarcoma&filter.overallStatus=RECRUITING|NOT_YET_RECRUITING&query.term=fusion+OR+transcription+factor+OR+degrader&pageSize=60). The same sentence's premise is also too strong: §2 says 'The large screens are fields-limited and carry no eligibility text', while the artifact's own instrument list describes ct_sarcoma_2026_new as 'unfielded so eligibility text is included'. One large screen does carry eligibility text, and it is the one that supplied the third record.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: These nine records are explicitly not adjudicated, so no admission or refusal in the paper rests on this retrieval. The count of three is right for 'has eligibility text'; it is the word 'individually' and the blanket claim about large screens that are wrong.
p1s.fix: 'eligibility text was retrieved for three of those nine, two of them individually and one inside an unfielded screen', and soften §2's 'the large screens ... carry no eligibility text' to 'the fielded screens'.
p1s.evidence: fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json, molecularly_defined_not_histology_defined[7].retrieved_from.source_url; task_2_widened_search.instruments entry for ct_sarcoma_2026_new

p1s.summary: Section 2 describes the transport defect as lost characters inside eligibility text, mitigated by not quoting. The artifact it rests on records TWO failure modes and names the one the paper omits 'SILENT and more dangerous': whole modules vanished from records that still parsed, and five payloads stopped parsing altogether. conditionsModule - the exact field this entire paper is about - is among the deleted modules.
p1s.where: Section 2, paragraph beginning 'The earlier read carried a transport defect.'
p1s.quote: 'The fetcher passed registry payloads through an HTML stripper, which deletes spans between angle brackets; the registry escapes comparison operators the same way, so eligibility text containing them lost characters.'
p1s.evidence: research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> transport_integrity. two_failure_modes[0]: 'LOUD: the deleted span crosses JSON structure and the record stops parsing.' two_failure_modes[1]: 'SILENT and more dangerous: the record still parses while whole modules have vanished.' silently_damaged_records lists NCT05836571 (three separate payloads), NCT01189253 and NCT04094610, each missing ['conditionsModule','designModule','eligibilityModule']. unparseable_records lists five payloads covering thirteen NCT ids - and two of the five ARE the diagnosis searches: ct_emc_all (query.cond=extraskeletal+myxoid+chondrosarcoma, lost NCT00720174 and NCT05355753) and ct_myxoid_chondrosarcoma (query.cond=myxoid+chondrosarcoma, lost NCT00720174, NCT05355753 and NCT01189253). The artifact's own instruments table says those payloads are what 'every study whose CONDITION list names EMC' was read from. So the defect was a COVERAGE defect in the paper's central measurement, not a quotation-hygiene defect, and the paper reports only the second. The re-fetch after the fix covered four candidate trials (the 2026-08-09 adjudication), not the condition searches, so the coverage was never restored.
p1s.note: Not a blocker on its own because the three dropped records turn out to be inert: research/modalities/emc-hypoxia-therapeutic-status.json records NCT00720174 COMPLETED, NCT05355753 TERMINATED and NCT01189253 TERMINATED. But that file is not named in section 7, so the paper's own cited set does not contain the evidence that closes the gap - see P1-4.
p1s.fix: State both failure modes and name the two condition-search payloads that were damaged; add one sentence to section 5 saying that the enumeration of trials whose condition list names the histology is incomplete by a known amount, and either re-fetch those two queries through the fixed fetcher or cite the artifact that resolves the three lost records.

p1s.summary: Section 2's stated reason for quoting no criterion from NCT05918640 is wrong, and it suppresses the paper's single best piece of evidence. The rule in the artifact is per-SENTENCE, not per-record, and the artifact carries a transport-clean verbatim criterion for exactly this trial.
p1s.where: Section 2, second sentence of the transport-defect paragraph.
p1s.quote: 'The rule applied at the time was that no sentence carrying a removal marker may be quoted, and it is why no criterion is quoted verbatim from NCT05918640, whose retrieved eligibility text carries one such marker and was not re-fetched after the fix.'
p1s.evidence: The rule, verbatim from research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> transport_integrity.rule_applied: 'No verbatim eligibility sentence is quoted in this file or in the draft notice unless THAT SENTENCE ITSELF carries no removal marker.' The same file's task_1_reverification_of_section_3_3 record for NCT05918640 carries removal_markers_in_eligibility_text = 1, and alongside it verbatim_sentence_is_transport_clean = true with verbatim_eligibility_sentence = 'Patients must have a known FET fusion (fusion that contains EWSR1, FUS, or TAF15) as documented by next generation sequencing, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) or Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH).' The paper turns a marker somewhere in the record into a bar on quoting the whole record, and the sentence it therefore withholds is the direct textual proof of its lead claim - that this trial's eligibility is written on the FET family.
p1s.fix: Quote the criterion, cite it as transport-clean, and restate the rule as the artifact states it. The paper's strongest evidence currently sits unused behind a misdescribed constraint.

p1s.summary: Section 7 says each of the three artifacts records the retrieval URL. Two of them do not, and one of the two says in terms that the URLs were never committed.
p1s.quote: 'Each records the retrieval URL, the run that fetched it and the date.'
p1s.evidence: research/literature/emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json: the only URL anywhere in the file is the API base inside retrieval.api, 'ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies)'; no adjudication entry carries a source_url, and retrieval.route states 'using the `targets_json` inline-manifest input - the urls were not committed anywhere, and `targets_file` names a path in the checked-out tree, so it could not have reached them'. research/literature/non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json: grep for 'http' returns nothing at all - the endpoints are named as registries ('ISRCTN (UK)', 'WHO ICTRP', 'EU CTIS', 'ANZCTR', 'jRCT') with a result code and no address. Only research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json satisfies the sentence, via per-record retrieved_from.source_url. Run id and date are present in all three; the URL clause is the false one.
p1s.fix: Say what is true: run id and date for all three, per-record retrieval URL for the 2026-08-07 sweep, and for the other two the API base plus the inline manifest that is not committed. Or commit the manifests and make the sentence true.

p1s.summary: Section 7 does not name every artifact the paper relies on. The paper's fourth NCT id and its clean-up depend on files section 7 omits, and the 42-condition record's own provenance is a targets manifest that is never named.
p1s.evidence: (a) NCT06239272, the record section 4.1 leans on, was fetched under the manifest research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c3.json ('ct_nct06239272_nrsts2021': 'https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT06239272?format=json'); section 7 names none of the three targets manifests (emc-clinical-sweep-targets.json, -c3.json, -c4.json) that the 2026-08-07 sweep's retrieval.runs block cites as its inputs. (b) The three trials the damaged condition searches dropped are resolvable only from research/modalities/emc-hypoxia-therapeutic-status.json (NCT00720174 COMPLETED, NCT05355753 TERMINATED, NCT01189253 TERMINATED), which section 7 does not name - so the paper's cited set does not contain what makes its section 4.1 negative safe. (c) The paper's claim that the defect 'has since been fixed at the fetcher' is a claim about scripts/lit_fetch_urls.py; I verified it (line 218 now reads 'NEVER RUN THE HTML STRIPPER OVER JSON/XML', commit 6b5fbc239), but the file is nowhere named.
p1s.fix: Name them. All three are already committed; this costs one sentence.

p1s.summary: The FET-family criterion admits most of this disease, not the disease. The paper's own cited artifact records two non-FET NR4A3 fusion partners, and a patient carrying one is outside NCT05918640's criterion. The paper says flatly that two trials 'admit this disease'.
p1s.where: Abstract ('Two recruiting interventional trials admit this disease and neither lists it'); section 3 table row 1 ('EMC's usual 5′ partner is a FET protein').
p1s.evidence: research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> task_2_widened_search._supporting_literature_read_in_the_same_ci_run, verbatim from the retrieved full text: 'In the vast majority of cases (over 70%), NR4A3 fuses to ... EWSR1 ... less frequently (about 20% of cases) to ... TAF15 ... Rarer (<5%) NR4A3 fusion partners include FUS ..., TCF12 ... and ... TFG'. The same block's note_for_the_reader: 'EWSR1, TAF15 and FUS are the three FET-family genes; TCF12 and TFG are not.' NCT05918640's criterion, verbatim: 'Patients must have a known FET fusion (fusion that contains EWSR1, FUS, or TAF15)'. A TCF12- or TFG-partnered NR4A3 fusion is therefore not admitted. The paper's word 'usual' in the table hedges the biology and does not reach the abstract's unqualified 'admit this disease'. I am deliberately not converting this into a percentage: >70 + ~20 + <5 does not sum to 100, the review does not separate FUS from TCF12/TFG inside its rarer group, and the artifact records that 'the primary series behind these percentages has NOT been traced'.
p1s.fix: One clause: the FET criterion admits EMC whose fusion partner is FET-family (EWSR1, TAF15 or FUS) and not EMC driven by a TCF12 or TFG fusion, which the cited review places inside its '<5%' rarer-partner group. The honest statement is the partner classes, not a derived percentage - the review's own figures do not sum to 100 and no primary series behind them has been traced (the artifact says so).

p1s.summary: The manuscript carries no literature identifier of any kind - zero PMIDs, DOIs, PMCIDs, ISRCTN ids. Its background medical claims are uncited, and the source that supports them is already sitting inside an artifact section 7 names.
p1s.where: Abstract, Background; section 3 table row 1; section 4.1.
p1s.quote: 'Extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EMC) is an ultra-rare sarcoma defined by an *NR4A3* fusion, most often EWSR1::NR4A3.' / 'EMC's usual 5′ partner is a FET protein.' / 'a cohort for *translocation-associated soft tissue sarcoma*, which EMC is'.
p1s.evidence: A regex sweep of the pinned document for NCT / ISRCTN / PMID / PMC / DOI / arXiv / GSE returns only four NCT ids and nothing else. The support exists and is anchored: research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> task_2_widened_search._supporting_literature_read_in_the_same_ci_run carries pmid 32967265, doi 10.3390/cancers12092703, pmcid PMC7563993, retrieved in Actions run 31176811772, with the verbatim partner-frequency sentence. I verified that identifier live through the PubMed MCP tool (the proxy 403s pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov): Stacchiotti S, Baldi GG, Morosi C, Gronchi A, Maestro R, 'Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma: State of the Art and Current Research on Biology and Clinical Management', Cancers (Basel) 2020;12(9), article_types ['Journal Article','Review'], whose abstract reads 'marked by a translocation involving the [NR4A3] gene, which can be fused in-frame with different partners, most often [EWSR1] or [TAF15]'. Source: PubMed. The artifact grades it 'SECONDARY - this is a review. Per systems/POLICY-evidence.md a review figure must not be presented as a primary study's', which is how it must be cited.
p1s.fix: Cite PMID 32967265 / DOI 10.3390/cancers12092703 for the fusion definition and the partner frequencies, marked as a review. The ISRCTN ids should also appear in section 4.1 - see P2-4.

p1s.summary: The 'listed conditions' column is the paper's load-bearing evidence, and for NCT06571734 it matches neither of the two artifacts section 7 names. The paper prints five entries; the 2026-08-09 adjudication records seven; the 2026-08-07 sweep records ten. Nothing reconciles the two artifacts and no ellipsis marks the truncation.
p1s.where: Section 3, table row 2; the same list is paraphrased in the Abstract.
p1s.quote: 'metastatic and unresectable leiomyosarcoma · bone sarcoma · translocation-associated soft tissue sarcoma · synovial sarcoma · osteosarcoma'
p1s.evidence: research/literature/emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json -> adjudications[0].listed_conditions = ['Metastatic Leiomyosarcoma','Unresectable Leiomyosarcoma','Bone Sarcoma','Translocation-associated Soft Tissue Sarcoma','Synovial Sarcomas','Osteosarcoma Metastatic','Ewing Sarcoma'] - seven. research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> task_2_widened_search.candidates_requiring_eligibility_text_verification, NCT06571734.listed_conditions = the same seven plus 'Ewing Sarcoma Metastatic', 'Sarcoma Metastatic', 'Sarcoma of Bone' - ten. The paper prints five, dropping 'Ewing Sarcoma' entirely and collapsing two leiomyosarcoma entries and the metastatic osteosarcoma entry. No claim inverts - 'EMC listed? no' is true on all three lists - but a reader who checks the paper's central exhibit against either cited artifact finds a mismatch, and the two artifacts disagree with each other by three entries with no note.
p1s.fix: Print the field as one artifact records it, date it, mark any truncation with an ellipsis, and add a line reconciling the 7-vs-10 difference (fields-limited screen on 2026-08-07 vs per-trial re-fetch on 2026-08-09) or say it is unexplained.

p1s.where: research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md (§2, the paragraph beginning 'The large screens are fields-limited')
p1s.what: Two sentences of the retrieval method are refuted by the artifact they rest on. (i) 'The large screens are fields-limited and carry no eligibility text, so they can identify a candidate and can never confirm one.' research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> task_2_widened_search.instruments records ct_sarcoma_2026_new as 'sarcoma + fusion/transcription factor/degrader, UNFIELDED SO ELIGIBILITY TEXT IS INCLUDED', and ct_ewsr1_term / ct_nr4a3_term as returning 'full records'; the same artifact's limits_of_this_screen scopes the fields-limited statement to 'The large screens (fusion, basket, sarcoma)' only. (ii) 'eligibility text was retrieved individually for three of those nine'. Of the three of nine carrying eligibility_text_retrieved true, only NCT05722886 and NCT03767075 have a retrieved_from.source_url of the per-study form https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/<NCT>?format=json. The third, NCT06988475, records payload ct_sarcoma_2026_new and source_url 'studies?query.cond=sarcoma&filter.overallStatus=RECRUITING|NOT_YET_RECRUITING&query.term=fusion+OR+transcription+factor+OR+degrader&pageSize=60' - a registry-wide screen, not an individual retrieval. NCT06988475 appears 0 times in research/literature/emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json. The paper's own §2 table defines 'individually' as 'every unconfirmed candidate re-fetched individually', so the word is not doing loose duty here.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: No adjudication moves. The nine are explicitly 'not adjudicated ... reported as molecularly defined and nothing more', and every admission and refusal in §§3-4 does rest on a per-trial retrieval. What breaks is the methods sentence, in the paragraph the paper uses to establish that its confirmations are per-trial - which is the paper's methodological selling point.

p1s.where: research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md (§3, final paragraph, first sentence; the claim is elevated in the Abstract as 'The sharpest result is an absence')
p1s.what: 'The driver gene is absent from the index entirely.' is contradicted by the next sentence of the same paragraph - 'A term search for it returns five studies' - and by research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> task_2_widened_search.nr4a3_is_absent_from_the_registry_index.studies, which lists five NCT records the term search returned. The gene is in the index; no trial is indexed to it as a subject. Worse for an absence claim, the instrument is not shown to enumerate: the same artifact's limits_of_this_screen says 'The registry-wide EWSR1 term search returns full records and is therefore capped by response size, not by pageSize: 7 studies came back for pageSize=100. It is a SAMPLE of EWSR1-indexed trials, NOT AN ENUMERATION' - and ct_nr4a3_term is the same instrument on the same URL shape (query.term=NR4A3&pageSize=100&format=json, 'full records for a registry-wide NR4A3 term search'). The artifact nowhere states that the NR4A3 return was complete. The paper carries no such caveat here, in the Abstract, or in §5, while calling the absence its sharpest result - the shape CLAUDE.md §4 names as an absent reading passed off as a reading of absence.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: The defensible form of the finding is already in the paper twice - 'No trial that search returns is indexed to this disease's driver' closes both the Abstract and §3 - so a one-word edit plus one caveat sentence keeps the result at full strength. The five returned studies are real and none is about this disease or any sarcoma.

p1s.where: research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md (§2 transport paragraph vs the §3 table row 1, the Abstract, and §5)
p1s.what: Half of the paper's headline count rests on a retrieval the paper itself flags as damaged, and the flag does not travel to where the claim is made. research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> confirmed_fusion_family_defined records NCT05918640 with removal_markers_in_eligibility_text 1 and no verbatim criterion; §2 discloses that marker, but only as the reason a quote is missing, and adds 'was not re-fetched after the fix'. Every other admission and refusal in the paper WAS re-fetched individually on 2026-08-09 (research/literature/emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json retrieval.all_four_returned 'HTTP 200'). §3's table then states NCT05918640's eligibility basis flatly, the Abstract states 'Two recruiting interventional trials admit this disease' with no qualifier, and §5 Limitations does not mention transport at all - so the reader who never reaches §2's third paragraph cannot know that one of the two admissions is the only load-bearing read that was never repeated with the fixed fetcher. The stripper deletes a span from '<' to the next '>', so what a removal marker hides is exactly a restricting clause, and the direction of that risk is toward overcounting admissions.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: The FET-family wording the admission turns on WAS present in the text that was read (the artifact's assessment quotes its reading of it), and the record is not among silently_damaged_records, so no module vanished. The claim is not shown false - it is shown to be resting on the one read that a $0 CI re-fetch would settle.

p1s.what: §4.1 states 'The mechanism therefore runs in both directions, WHICH IS THE FULLER RESULT' and then bounds the central claim - 'One record does both ... so nothing here says that no listing anywhere names this disease and admits it'. Neither half reaches the Abstract. The Abstract's 'What we found' reports only the admit-without-naming direction plus the NR4A3 absence, mentions the UK registry only under 'What we did', and never names the exclusion finding or NCT06239272. A reader of the Abstract alone takes away an unqualified 'eligible but unfindable' and never meets the record that lists the histology and is recruiting. The front matter compounds it: canonical_for names 'the 2026-08-09 EMC trial-reachability finding' in the singular, while the body says the fuller result is two-directional.
p1s.why_not_a_blocker: Both the finding and its bound are stated correctly in the body, and the Abstract makes no exhaustiveness claim that the bound falsifies. It is a coverage gap between abstract and body, not a false sentence.

p1s.summary: 'Two recruiting interventional trials admit this disease' (abstract) gives equal weight to an explicit verbatim molecular criterion and to a class-term reading the paper's own adjudication declines to make.
p1s.evidence: NCT05918640 carries a verbatim criterion naming the FET family — the admission is on the posted text. NCT06571734's admission rests on the cohort term 'translocation-associated soft tissue sarcoma', and emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json says of it, verbatim: "'Translocation-associated Soft Tissue Sarcoma' is not further enumerated in the retrieved criteria, so whether the investigators read it as a general class or as the three histologies they listed is NOT determinable from the registry record." The paper carries that caveat in §5 but the headline count does not reflect it, and the count is what a citing author will quote. 'Admit' also does the work of 'would accept', which §5 correctly says is not a registry fact.

p1s.summary: NCT05918640's eligibility text carries a transport removal marker and was never re-fetched after the fetcher was fixed. This is mentioned in §2 as the reason for not quoting, and is absent from §5 Limitations, where it belongs — it is a limitation on one of the two trials in the headline.
p1s.evidence: Paper §2: 'it is why no criterion is quoted verbatim from NCT05918640, whose retrieved eligibility text carries one such marker and was not re-fetched after the fix.' Deposit: removal_markers_in_eligibility_text = 1 for NCT05918640. The transport defect deletes spans between angle brackets, and the deposit's own two_failure_modes[1] names the silent mode — 'the record still parses while whole modules have vanished'. Re-fetching is a $0 CI call on a pipeline that has already been fixed and already been dispatched twice; a referee will ask why it was not.

p1s.summary: §3's 'listed conditions' column for NCT06571734 shows five terms; the deposit shows seven for the same trial on 2026-08-09 and ten on 2026-08-07. Three readings of the same field, none reconciled, in a paper whose entire thesis is what that field contains.
p1s.evidence: Paper §3: 'metastatic and unresectable leiomyosarcoma · bone sarcoma · translocation-associated soft tissue sarcoma · synovial sarcoma · osteosarcoma'. adjudication-2026-08-09 listed_conditions (7): + 'Ewing Sarcoma'. fet-fusion-2026-08-07 candidates_requiring_eligibility_text_verification listed_conditions (10): + 'Ewing Sarcoma Metastatic', 'Sarcoma Metastatic', 'Sarcoma of Bone'. The paper's row silently drops 'Ewing Sarcoma' with no ellipsis, and neither the paper nor either artifact notes that the two deposited reads disagree. The central claim is unaffected — emc_in_listed_conditions is false under all three readings — but a referee who checks one field and finds the deposit disagreeing with itself will re-check every other number.

p1s.summary: One of the nine records in §3's third row carries a RECRUITING flag last verified April 2024 and a deposited instruction to confirm with the site. The paper's §5 says only 'Statuses go stale. Every status here is as posted on the retrieval date.'
p1s.evidence: NCT03767075 (Basket of Baskets) — status_verified_date '2024-04', last_update_post_date '2024-04-25'; deposit assessment verbatim: 'its RECRUITING flag is over two years stale in the registry - confirm directly with the site.' The paper's abstract counts it inside 'Nine further registry records … name no histology either', with 'one of those not yet recruiting' as the only status qualification. A known specific caveat downgraded to a generic hedge is the failure mode this repository's own evidence discipline names.

p1s.summary: The abstract's 'Three further non-US registries refused automated access' and §5's 'two more refused automated access' count jRCT's SSL handshake failure as an endpoint policy refusal. The positive control cannot discriminate that from a client-side failure of our own, which is the same class of self-inflicted defect the paper correctly owns for the WHO URL.
p1s.evidence: non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json endpoints: EU CTIS 'HTTP 403', ANZCTR 'HTTP 403', jRCT 'SSL handshake failure'. A 403 is a server answering and denying — the positive control makes that reading sound. An SSL handshake failure means no HTTP conversation happened at all, and it is equally consistent with our client's TLS version, cipher suite, SNI, CA bundle or egress proxy. The paper's own §2 sentence — 'a positive control fetched in the same run returned normally, so those refusals are statements about those endpoints and not about our retrieval' — does not hold for a transport-layer failure. Either re-attempt jRCT with the handshake diagnosed, or move it beside the WHO URL as 'unread, cause not established'.

p1s.summary: §4.1: 'searching that registry for this histology returns two trials'. The executed ISRCTN query was the parent term 'chondrosarcoma', not the histology.
p1s.evidence: non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json → endpoints[0] ISRCTN queries: ['chondrosarcoma', 'sarcoma AND fusion']; the count of two comes from isrctn_what_it_holds.query_chondrosarcoma.total_count = 2. The deposit repeats the same mislabel in its own key name. The substantive conclusion is unharmed (a narrower query returns no more), but in a paper arguing that the exact search string decides what a patient finds, misdescribing which string was searched is a methodological error in its own subject matter.

p1s.summary: §6.1 asserts 'The information already exists in the protocol; it is simply not in the field that search reads.' For a FAMILY-defined criterion that is not true — the admitted-histology list does not exist and would have to be constructed by the sponsor, which is precisely the one-trial-at-a-time judgement §4 says cannot be automated. And the paper omits the record that most sharply tests the remedy.
p1s.evidence: NCT05918640 admits any tumour with an EWSR1/FUS/TAF15 fusion — a set spanning Ewing, DSRCT, clear cell sarcoma, myxoid liposarcoma, angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma, low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma, myoepithelial tumours and this histology; enumerating it is a new editorial act, not a transcription. The omitted counterexample is in the deposit: NCT07188532 LISTS a molecular condition — 'Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion', which literally describes EWSR1::NR4A3's class — and the paper's own §4 adjudicates it as REFUSING this disease. So a sponsor following Remedy 1's spirit produced exactly the false positive §4 warns about. The paper mentions this trial only as the 'extra-skeletal' keyword trap and never as the counterexample to its own remedy.

p1s.summary: The primary instrument for the paper's mechanism — the fusion screen — returned exactly its page limit and is therefore truncated. Nothing in the paper says its counts are lower bounds.
p1s.evidence: fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json → task_2_widened_search.instruments[0]: payload ct_fusion_recruiting_fixed 'returns 400 recruiting studies', against a source_url carrying pageSize=400 — saturated. (The basket screen returned 199 of 400 and the sarcoma screen 526 of 1000, so those two are not truncated; only the fusion one is, and it is the one that matters.) §2 says the large screens 'can identify a candidate and can never confirm one', which is about eligibility text, not about coverage. 'Two recruiting interventional trials admit this disease' reads as a census and is a floor.

p1s.summary: The word 'site' appears zero times; 'United States', 'Canada', 'Canadian' zero times; no sponsor, city or country anywhere. For a paper whose subject is whether a patient can reach a trial, indexing is only one of the barriers, and the deposit carries the others.
p1s.evidence: Grep of the pinned text: 0 hits for site/United States/Canada/Canadian/Philadelphia/Northwestern/St. Jude. Deposit: NCT05918640 is sponsored by Children's Hospital of Philadelphia with minimum_age '10 Years' (a paediatric centre, which is a practical barrier for an adult independent of the posted maximum age); NCT06571734 is Northwestern University with an NCI collaborator; NCT04151342 carries an explicit deposit field '⚠_geographic_limit: Participating sites are Canadian', which the paper drops when it repeats that trial in §3. Either state the scope ('reachability here means registry-indexing reachability only, not geographic or referral reachability') in §1 and §5, or carry the site facts.

p1s.summary: The paper's premise is what a patient's own diagnosis search yields, and it never reports that search's result set for the US registry — while the deposit records those exact payloads as containing unparseable and silently damaged records.
p1s.evidence: Deposit instruments[6]: 'ct_emc_full_fixed / ct_emc_all / ct_myxoid_chondrosarcoma — every study whose CONDITION list names EMC'. transport_integrity.unparseable_records: ct_emc_all → NCT00720174, NCT05355753; ct_myxoid_chondrosarcoma → NCT00720174, NCT05355753, NCT01189253. transport_integrity.silently_damaged_records: NCT05836571 and NCT01189253 lost conditionsModule, designModule and eligibilityModule in those same payloads. The paper reports exactly one record from this search (NCT06239272, in §4.1) and no total, no statuses and no note that the search's own payloads were damaged. Every absence claim about the US registry rests on this unreported, partly unreadable set.

p1s.summary: No denominator appears anywhere in the paper. The screen size, the instrument sizes and the number of trials actually adjudicated are all in the cited artifacts and none reaches the page, so no count in the paper can be placed against a base and the keyword-map counter-finding cannot be read as the 2-of-4 it is.
p1s.evidence: fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> retrieval.unique_studies_indexed = 1159; task_2_widened_search.instruments records 400 recruiting studies for the fusion screen, 199 for the basket screen and 526 for the sarcoma screen. emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json -> summary: candidates_adjudicated 4, admits_and_is_interventional 1, admits_but_is_observational 1, refused 2. The manuscript reports none of these. The abstract's 'Two recruiting interventional trials admit this disease' (line 56) and §4's 'Two candidates were adjudicated as not admitting this disease' (line 139) are counts without bases; a reader cannot tell whether four trials or four hundred were read, and cannot see that the paper's headline methodological result is two false positives out of four adjudications.

p1s.summary: Every count in the paper is a lower bound conditioned on a fielded keyword screen, and is written as a complete count. §2 states the confirmation limit of those screens and never the coverage limit, so the paper demonstrates keyword screening's false positives while its own numerator is exposed to that same instrument's false negatives.
p1s.evidence: §2 line 105-107: 'The large screens are fields-limited and carry no eligibility text, so they can identify a candidate and can never confirm one.' That is the confirmation half only. The instruments (task_2_widened_search.instruments) are query.term screens on 'gene fusion / fusion-positive / FET fusion / translocation', on 'basket / tumor agnostic / histology agnostic / rare tumors', and query.cond=sarcoma, each filtered to RECRUITING|NOT_YET_RECRUITING. A trial whose eligibility text admits a FET fusion or a translocation class but whose title, conditions and interventions carry none of those tokens could never enter the candidate pool, and §4 is the paper's own proof that fielded metadata and eligibility text disagree. Nothing in §5 names this. The abstract should read 'at least two', and §5 should carry the blind spot in the same sentence that carries the registry limit.

p1s.summary: §3's table is headed 'Trials admitting this disease without naming it' and its second column is 'why it admits', yet nine of the records in it are ones the paper itself says were not adjudicated, and the seven arms among them are keyed to alterations this disease does not carry.
p1s.evidence: emc-trial-reachability.md line 118 (heading), line 120 (column 'why it admits'), line 124 (the row). The nine are, from task_2_widened_search.molecularly_defined_not_histology_defined: NCT05722886 (DETERMINE master screening protocol), NCT03767075 (Basket of Baskets), and arms NCT05770037 Alectinib/ALK, NCT05770102 Atezolizumab, NCT05770544 Entrectinib, NCT05786716 Trastuzumab+pertuzumab, NCT05768178 Vemurafenib+cobimetinib, NCT06988475 Capmatinib/MET, NCT07440290 Dabrafenib+trametinib (NOT_YET_RECRUITING). None is keyed to a FET fusion, a translocation class or NR4A3, and the artifact's own assessment of the master reads 'Whether EWSR1::NR4A3 matches an open arm is a question for the trial team.' The row's own text says 'not adjudicated' and §2 line 107-109 repeats it, so the table heading and the column header assert on nine records what the body of the same row withdraws. The disclosure is present; the label a reader scans is not. A separate table, or a heading such as 'Records whose eligibility is molecular and whose conditions never name the histology', would carry the same evidence without importing nine records into an admitting set.

p1s.summary: The NR4A3 term search's completeness is unestablished - the paper's own file says the identical instrument on the sibling gene is a sample and not an enumeration - and §3 states its result as a property of the registry rather than of the search.
p1s.evidence: task_2_widened_search.limits_of_this_screen[0]: 'The registry-wide EWSR1 term search returns full records and is therefore capped by response size, not by pageSize: 7 studies came back for pageSize=100. It is a sample of EWSR1-indexed trials, not an enumeration.' The NR4A3 search is the same shape - nr4a3_is_absent_from_the_registry_index.search_url is https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies?query.term=NR4A3&pageSize=100&format=json, full records - and the block records five studies with no totalCount field, so five may be a page rather than a total. §3 line 131, 'The driver gene is absent from the index entirely', is stronger than a possibly-capped search can license and is contradicted by its own next sentence, which reports five records the index returns for that term. The scoped form at line 134-135, 'No trial that search returns is indexed to this disease's driver', is exactly right and SURVIVES; it is the sentence to keep, with the cap stated beside it.
